input.quote: 13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
input.rationale: Section 13 binds us (Clear Capital) as well as RadialSpark, so the preferred position of no non-solicit on the Customer is not met. However, the restriction is already mutual, is limited to personnel with direct involvement in the Services, runs only one (1) year post-termination (well inside the 24-month walk-away limit), and is a solicitation restraint rather than a no-hire, so it substantially matches our fallback. The single missing fallback element is the carve-out for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, which creates real breach risk from ordinary job postings and inbound candidates. Given the existing mutual bargain, deleting the clause outright would be disproportionate, so we propose the minimal fallback edit adding the carve-out sentence.

proposal.summary: Add general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs to the mutual non-solicitation clause.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We can live with this mutual, narrowly scoped non-solicit, but we need the standard carve-outs so that general job postings, recruiter searches not targeted at the other party, and unsolicited approaches by individuals do not create a breach. This tracks our playbook fallback position of a 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the Services with a general-advertising exclusion.

ops.oldText: without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
ops.newText: without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing in this Section shall restrict either party from (a) placing or responding to general advertisements, job postings or other recruiting efforts not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, including engaging search firms that conduct such general efforts, or (b) hiring or engaging any individual who approaches such party on an unsolicited basis or who responds to any such general recruiting effort.
